context:
Goal: stop the glossary check failing a backticked decision id.
Problem (rule): the check that each workflow thing keeps its one glossary name (lint/check_glossary.py) flags 7 of 359 backticked record ids, such as `owner-feedback-inbox` ("uses 'inbox'; the glossary name is 'mailbox'"); it reads names without regard to sense on purpose, and a test holds that.
Based on (read): the lane's test that shows the check failing on a cited record name, on its own branch.
Departs from: main flags a record's own name in a cite — a lets every such cite pass, b marks each of the 7 records to pass.

options.how: The check passes a backticked id of any record the repo holds. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.
options.label: Pass any cited record
options.lose: An old glossary word can hide inside an old record's cite.

options.gain: The check stays as strict as today for every other name.
options.how: Each of the 7 records gets a mark in its glossary row saying its name stays; the check keeps reading names without regard to sense.
options.label: Mark each record (Recommended)
options.lose: Each of the 7 needs a mark, and a new one later needs one too.

ref: coordinator 12:51 CST Nov 12 (its clock), from lane guard-false-alarm-cull
reply: Settled by your Oct 27 ruling (decision uniform-over-variants: a shared tool never grows a second accepted form): b. The 7 records each get a mark in their glossary row; the check stays as strict for every other name. No answer needed from you.
short: Glossary check vs cited record names
title: The glossary check stops failing a cited record's own name
why: It changes what a shared check accepts; the lane runs its other families meanwhile.
